transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I came in because… well, it sounds a little ridiculous when I say it out loud, especially since I’m a physician, you know, I’m used to telling people what’s rational and what isn’t. But the thought of getting on an airplane now scares me so badly. I know in my head it doesn’t make sense, but my body reacts like that plane is absolutely going to fall out of the sky.

And I keep thinking about it even when I’m not near an airport—sorry, I know I’m rambling. That’s basically why I’m here.

Is flying the only situation that causes you this kind of intense anxiety, or do you experience similar fears in other situations, like being in crowded places, leaving your home, or being in open spaces?

It’s really the airplane. I mean, crowded places can be annoying—like hospital cafeterias, conferences, all that—but that’s not the same thing. The thing that hits me is the thought of getting on a plane. I can tell myself it’s irrational, I know the statistics and all of that, but my body just… it reacts like the plane is going to fall. That’s the fear that brought me here.
When you think about flying, do you go out of your way to avoid it, or do you still fly but experience extreme anxiety when you do?

I avoid it, yes. Or I try to. I’ve canceled clinic coverage before because I couldn’t face a flight, and I’ve skipped medical meetings I probably should have gone to.

And my family is in Honduras, so… that’s been hard. I keep putting off seeing them because I can’t make myself go to the airport. If I do get that far, I’m shaking, and I need someone with me, like I’m holding onto them just to get through it. It’s embarrassing, honestly.
How long has this fear of flying been affecting you, and has it been consistent over time, or does it come and go?

It’s been about… seven months, I think. It started after this really turbulent small-plane flight, right after I’d lost my clinic job, which probably made the whole thing feel worse. I keep thinking, if that job situation hadn’t happened, maybe I would’ve brushed the flight off, but—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

Since then it’s been pretty consistent. It’s not like I’m fine one month and terrified the next. The fear has just kind of stayed there whenever flying comes up.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort, like panic attacks, in situations other than thinking about or being on a plane?

I don’t think so… not in that sudden, out-of-nowhere way. I mean, I get stressed, sure—medicine gives you plenty of chances for that, and sometimes even the hospital parking garage is its own kind of nightmare—but it’s not the same as what happens with flying.

When it’s a plane, or even the idea of the plane, that’s when it becomes this intense thing. Outside of that, I haven’t really noticed episodes like that.
Have you ever had a panic attack when you weren’t thinking about flying or being on a plane?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ve had stressful moments, like anybody—especially at work, you know, people can be very demanding, and then there’s paperwork and insurance forms and all that—but I wouldn’t call those panic attacks.

The really intense fear, the kind that feels like I can’t handle it, that’s tied to the flying situation. Outside of that, I haven’t noticed it happening.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, intense wave of fear or panic in situations unrelated to flying, even if it was brief and passed on its own?

I don’t think so… not that I can clearly point to. I mean, I’ve definitely had moments where I felt overwhelmed, but then I start thinking about whether that counts, because in medicine everyone throws around words like “panic” casually—patients say it, colleagues say it, I probably say it too when the EMR freezes.

But a sudden wave like that, unrelated to flying… I haven’t really noticed that happening. At least not in a way that stands out to me.
Have you ever had a panic attack while you were in a situation that wasn’t related to flying, like at home, at work, or in a car?

I don’t think I have, no. At home or work or driving, I get tense or irritated sometimes—work especially, because there’s always some new form or system that doesn’t work the way it’s supposed to—but it doesn’t turn into that kind of sudden panic.

At least, nothing that I’d recognize as a panic attack outside of the flying thing.
Have you ever had a panic attack while you were in a situation that wasn’t related to flying, like at home, at work, or in a car?

I mean, I think I’d say no—or at least I can’t think of a time. Like, at work I can get wound up, especially when the schedule is packed or something administrative goes sideways, but that’s more frustration than anything else.

At home or in the car… no, nothing really comes to mind that I’d call a panic attack. It’s hard because people use that word pretty loosely, but no, I haven’t noticed it outside the flying context.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, unexpected surge of fear or anxiety that peaked within minutes, even if it wasn’t related to flying?

Not really, no. I’m trying to think of something that would fit that—like suddenly out of nowhere and peaking fast—and I can’t come up with an example.

I mean, I’ve had stressful moments, sure. Medicine is full of those; sometimes half the day feels like you’re just reacting to things. But that’s more… workload, annoyance, pressure. Not this sudden unexpected surge you’re describing. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, unexpected surge of fear or anxiety that came out of nowhere and peaked within minutes, even if it wasn’t related to flying?

No, I don’t think so. I keep trying to sort of scan back for something like that, and I’m not coming up with anything.

I mean, there are definitely times I get stressed—especially at work, because there’s always some new policy or paperwork thing that somehow takes longer than seeing the actual patient—but that’s not really “out of nowhere.” That’s more me reacting to the day being ridiculous.

So… no, not that sudden wave you’re describing, at least not outside of flying.
Have you ever had a panic attack when you were completely relaxed or not expecting it, even if it wasn’t related to flying?

No… I don’t think I’ve had that. Like if I’m just sitting at home, watching something, or reading, I don’t suddenly get hit with panic out of nowhere.

I do get wound up about things, but usually there’s a reason I can point to. And honestly, when I’m actually relaxed, I’m usually more likely to fall asleep than panic—my wife jokes that I can fall asleep in a chair in about three minutes, which is probably not what you’re asking.

So, no, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you ever had a panic attack when you were not in any situation that scared you beforehand, like when you were just relaxing or going about your normal day without any obvious trigger?

No, I don’t think so. If I’m just going through a normal day or sitting around at home, I don’t suddenly get that kind of panic out of nowhere.

I mean, normal day is a funny phrase—some days at work are anything but normal—but even then, if I’m stressed, I usually know why. It’s not like I’m brushing my teeth or making coffee and suddenly my body decides there’s an emergency. My coffee maker does make this awful grinding noise sometimes, which is probably its own issue, but no… not a panic attack kind of thing.
